{{Quote|Ah, ah, ah, ah, ah, ah&mdash;we don't want to have to hurt anyone. That's not what we're here for. But when my men get angry&hellip; I can't always control them.|The commander, to Mallatobuck|<ref name="Holiday Special" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] '''commander''' in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Imperial Military/Legends|military]] helped enforce martial law on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] during an [[Blockade of Kashyyyk (1 ABY)|Imperial blockade]] of the world during the [[Life Day/Legends|Life Day]] [[holiday]] of [[1 ABY/Legends|1.5 ABY]]. Leading a team of two [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and a [[Unidentified Imperial technician|technician]], the [[Commander/Legends|commander]] entered residences of the planet's native [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] and searched for ties to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. When the Imperials arrived at the [[Chewbacca's home|house]] of the Alliance hero [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], who was away from home, they harassed [[Chewbacca's family/Legends|Chewbacca's family]] while awaiting his return, yet remaining ignorant of his identity. After dismissing the [[Merchant/Legends|trader]] [[Saun Dann]] from the house; threatening Chewbacca's [[Marriage/Legends|wife]], [[Mallatobuck/Legends|Mallatobuck]], with harm; and overseeing a search of the residence; the commander finally departed when Chewbacca's son [[Lumpawaroo/Legends|Lumpawarrump]] covertly used a [[mini-transmitter]] to broadcast a "return to base" signal to the [[Officer/Legends|officer's]] [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]]. Suspecting that their missing Wookiee was indeed a Rebel, the commander left stormtrooper [[B4711]] at the house to await Chewbacca's return.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Investigate the upper area. Check for any Rebel material. Anything to connect this household with the Alliance.|The commander, ordering a search of Chewbacca's home|<ref name="Holiday Special" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] with [[Color/Legends|brown]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]] and brown [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]<ref name="Holiday Special" /> served as a [[Commander/Legends|commander]]<ref name="EGTC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'' {{C|under "Chewbacca"}}</ref> in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Imperial Military/Legends|military]] during the Empire's [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|civil war]] with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. During the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[holiday]] of [[Life Day/Legends|Life Day]]<ref name="Holiday Special" /> midway through the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="Leland Holiday">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=870#15778940|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2006-10-12|time=6:13 PM}}</ref> the commander was dispatched to the Wookiee [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] during an [[Blockade of Kashyyyk (1 ABY)|Imperial blockade]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. Martial law was declared and a curfew imposed due to suspected Rebel activity on Kashyyyk, and the commander led two [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]]<ref name="Holiday Special" /> and a [[Unidentified Imperial technician|technician]]<ref name="EGTC" /> from home to home in search of ties to the Alliance. Their hunt brought them to a [[Chewbacca's home|treetop house]]<ref name="Holiday Special" /> in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Rwookrrorro/Legends|Rwookrrorro]]<ref name="Tyrant's Test">''[[Tyrant's Test]]''</ref> that belonged to the [[Chewbacca's family/Legends|family]] of [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]],<ref name="Holiday Special" /> an Alliance hero.<ref name="EGTC" />

[[File:Investigate_the_upper_area-SWHS.png|thumb|left|250px|The commander leads a search of Chewbacca's home.]]
The Imperials barged into the house and found three Wookiees: Chewbacca's [[Marriage/Legends|wife]], [[Mallatobuck/Legends|Mallatobuck]], his [[Parent/Legends|father]], [[Attichitcuk/Legends|Attichitcuk]], and his son, [[Lumpawaroo/Legends|Lumpawarrump]]. The Human [[Merchant/Legends|trader]] [[Saun Dann]] was also present. As the residents cowered, the [[Technician/Legends|technician]] reported that another adult male Wookiee lived in the home; although unaware that the Wookiee in question was<ref name="Holiday Special" /> the famous Chewbacca,<ref name="EGTC" /> the commander demanded to know where he was. Dann offered his services as a [[Translator/Legends|translator]] between the Imperials' [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] and the Wookiees' [[Shyriiwook/Legends|Shyriiwook]], but the commander was only interested in seeing the trader's identification. As he plugged Dann's [[Identichip/Legends|identification card]] into a [[Identification reader|reader]], he ordered his men to search the residence for any signs of Rebel activity. When the trader's card checked out, the commander dismissed him from the home, and a nervous Dann&mdash;who was also secretly a member of the Alliance, hoping to protect Chewbacca's identity&mdash;only departed when he found a stormtrooper's [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] pointed at his chest.<ref name="Holiday Special" />

The impatient commander bid his men to finish their search, but when one of the [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] pointed his [[Blaster rifle/Legends|rifle]] at a furious Mallatobuck after the other [[Troop/Legends|trooper]] knocked Lumpawarrump and Attichitcuk out of his way, the commander intervened. He ordered Mallatobuck to keep her son quiet, implying that harm would otherwise come her way. She cooperated by letting her son watch a [[Unidentified Rebel cartoon|cartoon]] about his father's adventures in the Rebellion, and when the video caused Lumpwarrump to scream, the commander investigated. The [[Youngling/Legends|young]] Wookiee quickly changed the screen of his [[video book]] to instead display a game, and the commander lost interest. Meanwhile, the technician and one of the troopers tore apart Lumpawarrump's room during their search, and the commander afterward sent the young Wookiee to clean it up, hoping that it would keep him out of the Imperials' way.<ref name="Holiday Special" />

All four Imperials directed their attention to the residence's [[wallscreen]] when a program began that announced itself as required viewing for all members of the Imperial forces. The program, entitled ''[[Life on Tatooine]]'', was a live broadcast of a harrowing night in the life of [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]], the nightshift [[Bartender/Legends|bartender]] of a [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|cantina]] in the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine's]] city of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]]. It was shown with the hope that viewers would be uplifted by a feeling of superiority over the [[Cantina/Legends|cantina's]] lowly denizens. Following the program, the commander's [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] transmitted a "return to base" order, which the Imperials failed to realize had actually been broadcasted by Lumpawarrump via a [[mini-transmitter]]. The commander led the technician and [[Unidentified stormtrooper (Blockade of Kashyyyk)|one stormtrooper]] out the door but left trooper [[B4711]] behind to await the return of the missing Wookiee. When Chewbacca did return, he and his Human companion, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], sent B4711 tumbling from the [[Tree/Legends|treetops]] down to the forest floor, and Saun Dann reported to [[Unidentified Imperial officer (wallscreen)|another Imperial officer]] that the stormtrooper had fled into the woods. The [[Imperial officer/Legends|officer]] believed the lie, and the Wookiees were free to celebrate Life Day without Imperial interference.<ref name="Holiday Special" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Finish the search of this house. We have other areas to cover today. You! ''Take the upper area!''|The commander, addressing his men and then losing patience with a stormtrooper|<ref name="Holiday Special" />}}
[[File:Belittling_Mallatobuck-SWHS.png|thumb|right|250px|The commander threatens Mallatobuck.]]
The Imperial commander had brown hair, brown eyes, and light skin. He wore prominent sideburns,<ref name="Holiday Special" /> which were popular with Imperial [[Officer/Legends|officers]] at the time.<ref name="JAS">''[[The Jedi Academy Sourcebook]]''</ref> While in Chewbacca's home, the commander was short with Saun Dann and had little patience for the trader's attempts to interfere with the search for Rebel activity. He displayed a similar temperament to his own men and grew annoyed with their slow progress, adamant that there were other homes to be searched before the [[Standard day/Legends|day's]] end. He frequently addressed his men with nothing more than a snap of his fingers.<ref name="Holiday Special" />

Although the commander prevented one of his stormtroopers from firing on Mallatobuck, he warned her not to test the trooper's patience, and subtly threatened her with harm unless she kept a reign on her son Lumpawarrump, whom the commander found annoying. Despite being unaware that he was in the home of Chewbacca, the commander suspected that the residence's missing Wookiee was one of the Rebels for whom he was searching, and acted on his suspicion by leaving B4711 behind after departing.<ref name="Holiday Special" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Factor in the song by Jefferson Starship, the holographic circus troupe, some ineffectual Imperial antagonists (including the Wilhelm-screaming stormtrooper, B4711), and it's no wonder the ''Star Wars'' Holiday Special is accused of having an identity crisis.|Alex Newborn|<ref name="Bad Feeling" />}}
The Imperial commander first appeared in ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'', a [[1978]] television feature that was [[Wikipedia:Spin-off (media)|spun off]] from the original [[1977]] [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'' film]].<ref name="Holiday Special" /> He was played by actor [[Jack Rader]].<ref name="actor">{{WebCite|url=http://starwarsholidayspecial.com/characters/imperial_guard_officer.htm|text=Imperial Guard Officer|work=[[Starwarsholidayspecial.com|The Star Wars Holiday Special]]|archivedate=20101223063848}}</ref> Although addressed only as "officer" in the program,<ref name="Holiday Special" /> and referred to as "Guard officer" in the fourth draft of the ''Holiday Special''{{'s}} script,<ref name="script">{{WebCite|url=http://starwarsholidayspecial.com/text/script.htm|text=The Fourth Draft Script &ndash; 09/13/78|work=[[Starwarsholidayspecial.com|The Star Wars Holiday Special]]|archivedate=20101223071504}}</ref> he was later identified as a commander in [[1995]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''.<ref name="EGTC" /> An Imperial commander was included in the ''Holiday Special'' as early as its initial story treatment, which features the character at an Imperial base, adamant with his [[Aide/Legends|aides]] that the ''Starship Musica'' [[Starship/Legends|vessel]]&mdash;carrying several Rebels&mdash;not be allowed to reach the Wookiee planet in time for holiday celebrations. A guest star, written to be played by actress [[Wikipedia:Raquel Welch|Raquel Welch]], volunteers to [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotage]] the ship.<ref name="story treatment">{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsholidayspecial.com/text/story_treatment.htm|text=Story Treatment, 05/31/78|work=[[Starwarsholidayspecial.com|The Star Wars Holiday Special]]|archivedate=20110716133502}}</ref>

Following its only airing, the ''Holiday Special'' was almost universally panned.<ref name="Jawa's Corner">{{InsiderCite|94|Jawa's Corner}}</ref><ref name="Bad Feeling">{{InsiderCite|106|I Have a Bad Feeling About This!}}</ref><ref name="farce1">{{WebCite|url=http://articles.latimes.com/2008/nov/16/entertainment/ca-starwars16|text=May the farce be with you (page 1 of 3)|work=[[Wikipedia:Los Angeles Times|Los Angeles Times]]|archivedate=20091010023132}}</ref> ''[[Star Wars]]'' author [[Alex Newborn]] has credited the Imperial characters as contributing factors to the program's poor finished product, calling them "ineffectual Imperial antagonists" in the midst of a 1970s [[Wikipedia:Variety show|variety show]] who helped lead to an overall lack of focus.<ref name="Bad Feeling" />

In the ''Holiday Special'', the commander wears three [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinders]] in his [[Imperial military uniforms/Legends|military uniform]] and sports a single row of six squares in his [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|rank insignia]].<ref name="Holiday Special" /> Although [[2012]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' explains the use of code cylinders and [[Military rank/Legends|rank]] insignia by officers of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]],<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> no source has revealed the branch of the Imperial Military to which the ''Holiday Special''{{'s}} commander belongs. His uniform's [[Clothing/Legends|tunic]] also parts down the middle,<ref name="Holiday Special" /> unlike the tunics worn by officers in the [[Original trilogy|original ''Star Wars'' trilogy]], which part down either the left or right side.<ref name="A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref><ref name="Empire">{{Film|V}}</ref><ref name="Jedi">{{Film|VI}}</ref>
